tasks.q: Put the stages of a device's life in order.
steps: The device is used and charged
The device is thrown away or recycled
tasks.fb: Most of the carbon is spent before the device is switched on for the first time.

tasks.q: Why is replacing a working phone every year an environmental issue?
a: Manufacturing is the biggest part of its footprint, so a new device repeats that cost
tasks.fb: Keeping a device longer is the single biggest thing a user can do.

tasks.q: Which of these are environmental impacts of manufacturing a device? Select all that apply.
opts: Energy used to mine and refine metals
Water used and polluted in processing
Carbon emitted shipping parts around the world
The size of the box it ships in
correct: Energy used to mine and refine metals
Water used and polluted in processing
Carbon emitted shipping parts around the world
tasks.fb: Packaging matters a little; mining and refining matter enormously.

tasks.q: Why are rare earth metals a particular concern?
a: They are hard to extract, the process is polluting, and supplies are concentrated in few places
They are only found in the UK
tasks.fb: Their name is misleading: they are not especially rare, but extracting them cleanly is hard.

tasks.q: A student says streaming costs nothing environmentally because the phone barely warms up. Why are they wrong?
a: The data centre and network doing the work use far more energy than the phone
Phones use more power than data centres
Video files are stored on the phone
tasks.fb: The cost moved; it didn't disappear.

tasks.q: Which change most reduces the carbon cost of running a data centre?
tasks.fb: Efficiency helps, but the source of the electricity dominates.

tasks.q: Why is e-waste dangerous in landfill?
a: Toxic metals such as lead and mercury leak into soil and water
tasks.fb: The harm outlasts the device by decades.

tasks.q: Why is exporting e-waste to poorer countries an ethical issue?
a: The health risk of stripping it by hand is moved to people with least protection
It is faster to recycle abroad
tasks.fb: The waste leaves, the harm doesn't.

tasks.q: Does each action mainly reduce the impact of manufacture, use or disposal?
items: Keeping a laptop for six years instead of three
Taking old machines to a certified recycler
Donating working computers to a charity
tasks.fb: Longer life attacks the largest share of the footprint.

tasks.q: Which has the greatest effect for one household?
a: Keeping devices for longer before replacing them
tasks.fb: Manufacturing dominates, so the fewer devices made, the better.

a: Manufacturing a new laptop emits far more carbon than three years of running the old one, so replacing them early increases the school's footprint
New laptops are bad for the environment

tasks.q: A question asks for the environmental impact of cloud storage. Which stage is most relevant?
a: Use, because data centres run continuously and consume large amounts of electricity
Manufacture, because servers are made of plastic
None: the cloud has no impact
tasks.fb: The cloud is a building full of computers somewhere.

tasks.q: Which stage of a device's life does each impact belong to?
items: Electricity drawn by a data centre
Water polluted near a processing plant
Workers stripping old boards by hand
Carbon from shipping components between factories
A school's machines left on overnight
Materials recovered by a certified recycler
Network equipment running day and night
tasks.fb: In the exam, name the stage and then the mechanism.

info.title: Most of it is made, not used
info.text: For a typical smartphone, manufacturing accounts for roughly three quarters of its lifetime carbon.

info.title: Gold in the bin
info.text: A tonne of discarded phones contains far more gold than a tonne of ore from a mine, which is why recycling them properly is worth doing.

info.title: Right to repair
info.text: Rules now require manufacturers of some products to supply spare parts for several years, driven exactly by the argument in this lesson.

info.title: Data centre thirst
info.text: Large data centres use water as well as electricity for cooling, which has become contentious in dry regions.

info.title: E-waste scale
info.text: Tens of millions of tonnes of electronic waste are produced each year, and only a fraction is formally recycled.

info.title: The best upgrade
info.text: Adding memory or an SSD to an older machine costs a fraction of the carbon of a new one, and is often the bigger speed gain.
